concepts.evidence: Those vectors drawn as arrows are particular points, often called a basis or spanning set of vectors, over which we aim to represent every other point in the space.

we will assume that our dataset has been mean-centered: a simple and completely reversible operation that involves subtracting off the mean of the dataset along each input dimension so that it straddles the origin.

we can form an associated Least Squares cost function
An orthonormal basis or spanning set is a very special kind of spanning set whose elements (i) have unit length, and (ii) are perpendicular or orthogonal to each other.
the autoencoder formula since it expresses how a point xp is first encoded (via wp = CTxp) and then decoded back to itself (Cwp = CCTxp).
the decoding Cwp is precisely the projection of xp onto the subspace spanned by C.

the linear Autoencoder cost function in Equation (8.17). We can think of this Least Squares as enforcing the Autoencoder formula shown in Equation (8.14) to hold when properly minimized, and thus it is often referred to as the linear Autoencoder.

Principal Component Analysis, or PCA for short, in practice.
the covariance matrix is defined as the N × N matrix 1/P X X^T.
